notes: such things as these divides between the comparative כְּ, which takes the correlative such ... as headed on the closing connective, and the substantival demonstrative, which takes the supplied things with these (rules 25, 31).
would is the fronted question auxiliary of the interrogative הֲ under rule 17, leaving the verb its own it have been well pleasing headed on the complement (rule 44).

הַיּוֹם fuses as to day under rule 30's one-rendering condition, headed on the noun, while the earlier הַיּוֹם is split because the ASV writes this day as two words, the article taking the demonstrative under rule 41.
